decision_conditions:
Reason : 1 - The siting, scale, form and massing of the extensions would be overly dominant and out of keeping when viewed in relation to the existing dwelling and site surroundings. Accordingly, the proposal would conflict with NPPF 2024, London Plan Policy D4 and Merton Local Plan 2024 Policies D12.3 and D12.4 due to the harm identified.
Reason : 2 - The proposed development, by reason of its siting, scale, form and massing, would fall contrary to Merton Local Plan Policies D12.3 and D12.4 in respect of neighbouring amenity causing an unacceptable impact on the outlook and light to numbers 45, 49 and 51 Faraday Road. 
Reason : 3 - INFORMATIVE
Note to Applicant
In accordance with paragraph 38 of the NPPF, The London Borough of Merton  (LBM) takes a positive and proactive approach to development proposals focused on solutions. LBM works with applicants/agents in a positive and proactive manner by:
"	Offering a pre-application advice and duty desk service. 
"	Where possible, suggesting solutions to secure a successful outcome.
"	As appropriate, updating applicants/agents of any issues that may arise in the processing of their application.
In this instance:
"	The application was not considered to comply with the provisions of the Development Plan and NPPF2024  as submitted, and would have required substantial changes such that a new application would be required. 
"	The application was considered to be fundamentally contrary to the provisions of the Development Plan and the NPPF,2024 and there were not considered to be any solutions to resolve this conflict. 
"	It is noted that the applicant/agent did engage in a pre-application discussions.
"	The applicant is advised to seek pre-application advice on any resubmission.
description: The construction of a two-storey rear extension of 2.5m over the ground floor, at first and second floor level to provide enhanced bedroom and bathroom space.
